analysis.title: European Conference: What Companies Said About The Macro Outlook
key_insights: Day one of the UBS European Conference points to resilient but uneven growth, persistent inflation and rising reliance on productivity gains to drive earnings. European activity is stabilising rather than accelerating.
Corporate confidence is relatively strong despite subdued underlying demand, so earnings growth may increasingly outpace economic growth.

Inflation in energy, raw materials and distribution continues (Essity, Mondi, Siemens Healthineers, Magnum Ice Cream), but managements expect to recover costs through pricing and efficiency. Holcim expects a significantly positive price-cost spread in 2027 and IAG can now pass through about 80% of fuel costs.
UBS sees inflation as possibly slower to normalise than expected, with corporate margins staying resilient as costs are passed to customers.

European recovery is selective. Holcim sees improving German construction, ArcelorMittal expects steel orders to recover as destocking ends, and ABB and Schneider Electric see early industrial improvement. Vodafone struggles in Germany, Rightmove sees a challenging UK property market, and Primark reports softness across continental Europe.
Infrastructure investment is providing more support to Europe than consumer demand.

AI and electrification are driving a two-speed economy. Schneider Electric cited 18-24 months of data centre demand visibility and potential capacity shortages in 2028. ABB reported sustained electrification demand and Vinci sees power transmission opportunities.
BHP and Antofagasta continue to invest in copper capacity, reflecting expected electrification demand.

Consumer spending is resilient but selective. Tesco is gaining share with strong premium products and Primark reported improving UK trading. Diageo expects North American weakness to persist into 2027, and European retail remains challenging.
Travel is comparatively resilient, with IAG, Air France-KLM and Accor reporting encouraging business travel or booking trends.

European banks gave constructive messages. NatWest expects sustained credit growth and BNP Paribas sees improving profitability with limited impact from French political uncertainty on corporate activity.
Santander expects its cost-income ratio to fall from 45% in 2025 to 36% by 2028, helped by AI, restructuring and integration.
China remains a weak end-market for Diageo and Siemens Healthineers, though Chinese competition and innovation create opportunities in automotive distribution and pharmaceuticals.

Stellantis, Vodafone, Santander and BNP Paribas stressed cost savings, automation and restructuring as key earnings drivers. Companies are leaning on productivity, pricing and capital discipline rather than volume growth.

sector_views.rationale: AI, energy infrastructure and electrification are creating a strong investment cycle, with Schneider Electric citing 18-24 months of data centre demand visibility.
Credit conditions look resilient and AI-driven efficiency gains could support profitability without stronger growth.
Spending is holding up but is selective, favouring value, differentiated brands and travel over some discretionary categories.
Copper capacity investment reflects expected electrification demand, while European steel and construction show early signs of recovery.

earnings_insights: Santander guides to a cost-income ratio of 36% by 2028, down from 45% in 2025.
Holcim expects a significantly positive price-cost spread in 2027, per management commentary at the conference.
Diageo expects North American weakness to persist into 2027, per management commentary at the conference.
UBS says earnings growth may increasingly outpace economic growth, driven by productivity gains.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A management target. AI and restructuring are expected to lift bank profitability without requiring stronger growth.
Airlines can now recover most fuel cost increases through pricing, which supports margins.

risk_factors: Inflation in energy, raw materials and distribution may normalise more slowly than expected.
European demand is subdued and the recovery is uneven.
Data centre capacity shortages are possible in 2028.
North American weakness at Diageo is expected to persist into 2027.
geopolitical: BNP Paribas sees limited impact from French political uncertainty on corporate activity.
China remains a weak end-market for Diageo and Siemens Healthineers.
